q: To love at all is to be vulnerable. Love anything and your heart will be wrung and possibly broken.
In the end, only three things matter: how much you loved, how gently you lived, and how gracefully you let go of things not meant for you.
We are all longing to go home to some place we have never known, except in the sacred space between two people.
Tell me, what is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life?
Death is not the opposite of life, but a part of it.
The measure of a life, after all, is not its duration, but its donation.
Grief is the price we pay for love.
To be deeply seen by someone, then, and be loved anyhow—this is a human offering that can border on miraculous.
Perhaps all the dragons in our lives are princesses who are only waiting to see us act, just once, with beauty and courage.
We are held together by the invisible threads of memories and quietly shared moments.
When someone you love dies, you do not lose them all at once. You lose them in pieces over a long time—the way the mail stops coming.
Love is the only reality and it is not a mere sentiment. It is the ultimate truth that lies at the heart of creation.
The reason it hurts so much to separate is because our souls are connected.
There is a land of the living and a land of the dead and the bridge is love, the only survival, the only meaning.
It is not length of life, but depth of life.
Death is a distant rumor to the young, but a close companion to the old.
A friend is someone who knows all about you and still loves you.
We are all travelers in the wilderness of this world, and the best we can find in our travels is an honest friend.
In the depth of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer.
How lucky I am to have something that makes saying goodbye so hard.
The love we give away is the only love we keep.
You do not have to be good. You do not have to walk on your knees for a hundred miles through the desert repenting. You only have to let the soft animal of your body love what it loves.
Loved ones never truly leave us; they sit quietly in the spaces between our thoughts.
There is no remedy for love but to love more.
We are born alone, we live alone, we die alone. Only through our love and friendship can we create the illusion for the moment that we're not alone.
The ultimate lesson all of us have to learn is unconditional love, which includes not only others but ourselves as well.
At the touch of love everyone becomes a poet.
To be loved deeply gives you strength, while loving someone deeply gives you courage.
A mother's arms are made of tenderness and children sleep soundly in them.
The bond that links your true family is not one of blood, but of respect and joy in each other's life.
Grief, I’ve learned, is really just love. It’s all the love you want to give, but cannot.
We don't remember days, we remember moments.
To live in hearts we leave behind is not to die.
When we love, we always strive to become better than we are.
Sometimes the smallest things take up the most room in your heart.
The best and most beautiful things in the world cannot be seen or even touched - they must be felt with the heart.
When you are sorrowful look again in your heart, and you shall see that in truth you are weeping for that which has been your delight.
Love does not consist in gazing at each other, but in looking outward together in the same direction.
You are watching other people live while your own life passes by in silence.
Checking your likes is the new smoking.
Simply put, humans are not wired to be constantly wired.
An endless bombardment of news and gossip and images has rendered us manic information addicts.
Incessant clicking and scrolling generates a background hum of anxiety.
We live in a culture where attention is the ultimate currency, but we give ours away for pennies to algorithm gods.
Put down the glow of the screen and step out into the quiet truth of the night sky.
Solitude is where you find yourself; social media is where you lose yourself in the crowd.
The price of anything is the amount of life you exchange for it.
All of humanity's problems stem from man's inability to sit quietly in a room alone.
The urge to refresh your feed is a nervous twitch that shatters uninterrupted time into shards too small for intentional living.
We eagerly signed up for what Silicon Valley was selling, but soon realized we were accidentally degrading our humanity.
Almost everything will work again if you unplug it for a few minutes, including you.
Nothing on a screen will ever replace the warm weight of a hand held in silence.
Disconnection is not a loss of signal; it is the recovery of your real life.
We are drowning in information, while starving for wisdom.
Face-to-face conversation is the most human and humanizing thing we do.
We think we are staying connected, but we are actually burying ourselves in digital isolation.
In a world of noise, quiet is a revolutionary act.
Your attention is your life. Whatever you give your attention to becomes your reality.
Do not let the machine decide what is worthy of your gaze.
Distraction is the thief of depth.
When you lose the ability to sit in silence, you lose the ability to know who you are.
Stop documenting the moment and start inhabiting it.
A deep life is a good life.
You cannot find yourself in a notification dot.
We trade hours of unrepeatable sunlight for pixels on a glass rectangle.
Boredom is the birthplace of creativity; do not kill it with a scroll.
Look up. The clouds are putting on a masterpiece that no screen will ever render.
The world is waiting outside your notifications.
You don't need to know what everyone is thinking all the time. Protect your inner peace.
In an age of speed, nothing could be more invigorating than slowness.
The screen gives us everything to look at, but nothing to hold.
Reclaim your leisure from low-grade digital distractions and give it back to your soul.
Clarity about what matters provides clarity about what does not.
Silence is not the absence of sound, but the presence of everything.
To be everywhere is to be nowhere.
Gratitude unlocks the fullness of life. It turns what we have into enough, and more.
Wear gratitude like a cloak, and it will feed every corner of your life.
Piglet noticed that even though he had a Very Small Heart, it could hold a rather large amount of Gratitude.
When you arise in the morning think of what a privilege it is to be alive, to think, to enjoy, to love.
There are only two ways to live your life. One is as though nothing is a miracle. The other is as though everything is a miracle.
Enjoy the little things, for one day you may look back and realize they were the big things.
Cultivate the habit of being grateful for every good thing that comes to you, and to give thanks continuously.
He is a wise man who does not grieve for the things which he has not, but rejoices for those which he has.
It is not happy people who are thankful; it is thankful people who are happy.
Drink your tea slowly and reverently, as if it is the axis on which the earth revolves.
For it is in giving that we receive.
To acknowledge the good that you already have in your life is the foundation for all abundance.
When I started counting my blessings, my whole life turned around.
The soul that gives thanks can find comfort in the quietest room and joy in the simplest meal.
Do not spoil what you have by desiring what you have not; remember that what you now have was once among the things you only hoped for.
Gratitude turns ordinary meals into feasts, routine jobs into joy, and strangers into friends.
Every morning we are born again. What we do today is what matters most.
Notice the quiet miracle of breathing in without pain, of drinking cold water when you are thirsty.
Blessed are those who can see cruel things in quiet places where other people see nothing.
Gratitude is the healthiest of all human emotions. The more you express gratitude for what you have, the more likely you will have even more to express gratitude for.
I would maintain that thanks are the highest form of thought; and that gratitude is happiness doubled by wonder.
Be thankful for what you have; you'll end up having more. If you concentrate on what you don't have, you will never, ever have enough.
The unexamined meal, the unappreciated breath, the forgotten sunset—these are the silent losses of an ungrateful life.
Let us be grateful to the people who make us happy; they are the charming gardeners who make our souls blossom.
In ordinary life, we hardly realize that we receive a great deal more than we give, and that it is only with gratitude that life becomes rich.
At times, our own light goes out and is rekindled by a spark from another person.
To feel grateful and not express it is like wrapping a present and not giving it.
May you notice today that the sun rose just for you, and the warm air on your skin is a gift with no price attached.
Rest and be thankful.
Silent gratitude isn't much use to anyone.
The deepest craving of human nature is the need to be appreciated.
Living in a state of gratitude is the closest thing to heaven on earth.
When you wake up, take a deep breath and give thanks for one more day on this beautiful, strange earth.
Gratitude makes sense of our past, brings peace for today, and creates a vision for tomorrow.
Enough is a feast.
There is a quiet majesty in simply waking up unharmed in a warm bed.
The roots of all goodness lie in the soil of appreciation for goodness.
Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner.
You have power over your mind - not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
I have often wondered how it is that every man loves himself more than all the rest of men, but yet sets less value on his own opinion of himself than on the opinion of others.
What others think of you is none of your business.
Your worth is not measured by the applause of a crowd that does not know your name.
If you seek approval from others, you offer them a leash to lead you wherever they wish.
A flower does not think of competing with the flower next to it. It just blooms.
To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.
Never trade your authenticity for approval.
It is not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.
The privilege of a lifetime is to become who you truly are.
Stop playing for the audience; play for the musician inside you.
When you are content to be simply yourself and don't compare or compete, everyone will respect you.
He who lives by the praise of others will die by their criticism.
Your inner scoreboard is the only metric that matters at the end of the day.
Don't promise when you're happy, don't reply when you're angry, and don't make decisions based on the applause of strangers.
I am not what happened to me, I am what I choose to become.
To be controlled by the opinions of others is to be a slave without chains.
If you live for their acceptance, you will die from their rejection.
The individual has always had to struggle to keep from being overwhelmed by the tribe.
Do not ask for permission to be who you were born to be.
How much time he gains who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does or thinks.
Unboastful confidence speaks in silence; loud insecurity begs for an audience.
You do not need to prove your existence to anyone. You are already here.
Self-worth comes from self-approval, not social approval.
The moment you stop looking for confirmation outside yourself, you step into your true power.
Be quiet inside yourself and let the world make its noise outside your fortress.
Because one believes in oneself, one doesn't try to convince others.
True freedom is having nothing to prove, nothing to hide, and nothing to protect.
Your opinion of yourself is your destiny.
Validation sought from the outside is a bucket with a hole in the bottom.
Stand tall in your own light, even if no one turns their head to see you.
When you don't need praise, you cannot be broken by blame.
It takes courage to grow up and become who you really are.
You were not born to live up to the expectations of others.
If you don't design your own life plan, chances are you'll fall into someone else's plan. And guess what they have planned for you? Not much.
True strength is quiet; it does not need to shout for attention.
